title: Triangle types & properties
examples: What is the rule for the angles inside a triangle?
How do I know if a triangle is isosceles?
If two sides are equal, what kind of triangle is it?

explain.say: Today we learn about different types of triangles. We will look at their sides and angles.
A scalene triangle has three sides of different lengths. No two sides are the same length.
An isosceles triangle has at least two sides that are equal in length. This is a key rule to remember.
An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal in length. It is a special type of isosceles triangle.
The sum of the angles in any triangle is always exactly one hundred and eighty degrees. This is a constant rule.

faq.q: How many equal sides must an isosceles triangle have?
faq.a: An isosceles triangle must have exactly two sides that are equal in length. It can have more than two, but at least two must match.
asks: What is the rule for two equal sides?
Does it need exactly two equal sides?

faq.q: If all three sides are equal, what is the triangle called?
faq.a: If all three sides are equal, the triangle is called an equilateral triangle. This means all its angles are also equal.
asks: What is the name for three equal sides?
What kind of triangle has three equal sides?

faq.q: Does the angle sum rule work for all shapes?
faq.a: No, the angle sum rule only works for triangles. For other shapes like quadrilaterals, the sum is different.
asks: Is 180 degrees always the answer for angles?

faq.q: Can a triangle be both isosceles and equilateral?
faq.a: Yes, it can be both. An equilateral triangle is a special case of an isosceles triangle because it has at least two equal sides.
asks: Can a triangle fit both descriptions?

faq.q: If I know two angles, can I find the third?
faq.a: Yes, you can find the third angle by subtracting the sum of the two known angles from one hundred and eighty degrees.
asks: How do I find the missing angle?
If I have 50 and 70 degrees, what is the third?

facts: A scalene triangle has three sides of different lengths.
An isosceles triangle has at least two sides of equal length.
An equilateral triangle has three sides of equal length.
The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always one hundred and eighty degrees.

quiz.say: A triangle has sides measuring five centimeters, seven centimeters, and eight centimeters. What type of triangle is it?
quiz.why: Because all three side lengths are different, the triangle is scalene.

wrong.0: This is wrong because all three sides are not equal to each other.
wrong.1: This is a different type of triangle based on angles, not sides.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might see two numbers that look similar.

quiz.say: Two angles in a triangle measure forty degrees and sixty degrees. What is the measure of the third angle?
quiz.why: You subtract the sum of the two angles from one hundred and eighty degrees.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you subtracted the two angles from each other.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you forgot to subtract the two known angles.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only added the two angles together.

quiz.say: If a triangle has two equal sides and angles of sixty degrees, sixty degrees, and sixty degrees, what is it?
quiz.why: If all three angles are sixty degrees, all three sides must be equal, making it equilateral.

wrong.0: This is wrong because two angles are equal, meaning two sides must be equal.
wrong.1: This is wrong because none of the angles measure ninety degrees.
wrong.3: This is correct but not the most specific answer; equilateral is better.
